The main takeaway from our work is that
α2δ‐ 1 plays a crucial role in the interaction of muscle with the extracellular environment, independently of its role in Ca2+ channel gating.

α2δ1 plays a dual function in muscle: (i) a role in EC coupling through its interaction with the β1a and Cav1.3 subunits and (ii) a role in the adhesion of myoblasts to the extracellular matrix through its interaction with αv integrins.
